what_this_is: Quantity-only and PROVISIONAL: the second number's two sensitivity scenarios (Joe, 2026-11-19, D-107; R2 of D-106) on the design as it stands on 2026-11-19, with the per-state reconstruction check that comes first, the sites and rows each moves, each state's factor, and the sample differences from the primary run. The plan is a DRAFT and not frozen. No price, revenue or bill was read; no estimate is here. They are sensitivity scenarios, not bounds or necessarily one-change comparisons with the primary analysis.
reading_of_report_sample_differences: the session's reading, Joe's to strike: for each scenario, every utility in its sample that is not in the primary run's and the reverse, by name, with its dose at each form; the class given is the utility's class in the primary classification at each form, since a single history defines no classes of its own (the agent's reading)

sensitivity_scenario_a_runner_up_placeme.label: Sensitivity scenario A, runner-up placement (Joe, D-107; R2 of D-106): every unresolved load-carrying site moved to the first other candidate that can hold its full load under the inventory's own placement rule, every date, capacity and basis as the inventory has it, each state's factor recomputed. Under Joe's rule (D-111) for what a candidate already carries, the 460 unresolved sites are lifted first, all other load kept counted, and placed in descending size, each counting where it lands; matching the earlier count is not the reason for the rule. Umatilla enters at 25.0 and 50.0 points at the caps (462 uncapped) and Portland General at 18.8 points. Besides its own kind of question it differs from the primary run in three ways: the two sites with no load history carry load at the early end of each of their questions (bi:852-0 from 2024; bi:837-0's date and the rest of its capacity at 2011), where the primary run leaves out every utility they reach; Oregon's factor is recomputed with those sites carrying load; and its sample differs (Portland General and Umatilla enter at the dose this history gives them, and any unit with load in this history and no 2009-2011 base leaves). It is a sensitivity scenario, not a bound and not necessarily a one-change comparison with the primary analysis.

units_whose_load_differs_from_the_recons.what: against the reconstruction at every setting of the inventory (realise with no settings), in which the two sites with no load history already sit at their early end, so the count is what this scenario's own kind of question moves; the reconstruction equals the dose file for every unit no load-unknown site reaches (the check)

sensitivity_scenario_a_runner_up_placeme.rule: What a candidate already carries (Joe's rule, adopted on 2026-11-19, D-111): "lift the 460 unresolved sites first, keeping all other load counted, then place them in the adopted descending-size order". Adopted on the condition, met, that a check made first and apart from the module found that lifting first neither introduces a capacity exceedance nor increases a pre-existing one (docs/gate1/scenario-a-exceedance-check-2026-11-19.md). Matching the earlier count is not the reason for the rule. A site for which no other candidate fits, or with no other panel candidate, stays where it is and counts on its unit from its own turn in the order. That clause stands by Joe's ruling of 2026-11-20 (D-113), and no further placement variant is tested; counting it only after every site is placed was not tried. Against the earlier reading (every site counted where it sat until it moved), 27 sites change destination and one more site moves (docs/gate1/scenario-a-count-reconciliation-2026-11-19.md).

sensitivity_scenario_b_other_end_of_ever.label: Sensitivity scenario B, the other end of every dated interval (Joe, D-107; R2 of D-106): each date entry in force that has a convention at the end of its interval its convention does not sit at, every assignment as the inventory has it, each state's factor recomputed. Umatilla enters at 0.0 points at both caps (316 uncapped) and Portland General at 18.9 points. Besides its own kind of question it differs from the primary run in three ways: the two sites with no load history carry load at the early end of each of their questions (bi:852-0 from 2024; bi:837-0's date and the rest of its capacity at 2011), where the primary run leaves out every utility they reach; Oregon's factor is recomputed with those sites carrying load; and its sample differs (Portland General and Umatilla enter at the dose this history gives them, and any unit with load in this history and no 2009-2011 base leaves). It is a sensitivity scenario, not a bound and not necessarily a one-change comparison with the primary analysis.

dependency_on_the_ownership_repair.why: the scenario sample is second_number.build_frame over every panel unit less the price hold (usability, market region, size band) and the doses are realised loads over sales; no design, eligibility list, matched set or ownership table is read. The primary classes are read from second_number_design.json's per-utility classes, which come from doses and histories only.

uncertain: I am uncertain whether the capacity test's starting load matches what the build used before its overrides: the rule here starts from what each candidate carries in the inventory as assigned less the 460 sites being placed (every other site on it, at its scaled full load, as pick_utilities counts load) and adds each of the 460 where it lands; build_inventory.pick_utilities started from nothing and placed every site in one pass before the overrides. The rule is stated, not a replication.
Whether Texas's factor moves under B: it is clipped at 3.0 in the inventory; the factor recomputed under B is reported in the factor table, and the raw factor before the clip is not reported.
